title: Qajar Dynasty
capsule: The Qajar dynasty was a Turkic-origin ruling house that governed Iran from 1789 to 1925, founded by Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar, who reunified Iran after the civil wars following Nadir Shah's death and was crowned Shah in 1796. The dynasty's long reign witnessed the Russo-Persian Wars of 1804–13 and 1826–28, under the Treaties of Gulistan and Turkmenchay respectively, which stripped Iran of the Caucasus provinces and imposed capitulatory privileges; the concurrent Anglo-Persian competition over Afghanistan further constrained sovereignty. Constitutional Revolution pressures in 1905–11 forced a Majlis (parliament) on the reluctant Qajar shahs, and after World War I's foreign occupations fully exposed the dynasty's weakness, Reza Khan's 1921 coup and 1925 Majlis vote ended Qajar rule and inaugurated the Pahlavi dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Iran's external borders under the Qajars are relatively well-documented through Russian and British diplomatic and survey records, particularly post-1828 treaty boundaries; internal tribal zones and the precise Afghan borderland are less definitively mapped for earlier decades.
